task.description:
Combined Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) per WF-03_issue_resolving.md. Claim this handoff by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.

Step 0.5: search docs/issues/*.yaml for a status: resolved entry with similar symptoms (empty/missing prefix guard, cross-endpoint cursor isolation). State whether a prior match was found.

Step 1: Reproduce directly -- write and run a throwaway script/test (e.g. `iex -S mix` or a scratch test) calling Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 with prefix: "" against a cursor minted with a different real prefix (e.g. one of the module's existing @*_cursor_prefix constants from lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex or similar), and show it succeeds when it should be rejected. Quote the real output. Then trace root cause in check_prefix/2 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex ~line 211-218): the size+starts_with? guard is vacuously true for prefix = "". Confirm via grep that every current real call site (lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex) passes a non-empty hardcoded module-attribute prefix (so no current caller is itself buggy -- this is a missing defense-in-depth guard, not a currently-exploited bug). Do NOT implement the fix -- produce the diagnosis (root cause, affected function/file, what a fix needs to change: check_prefix/2 must reject prefix == "" outright) for CODE-DESIGNER to design from.
acceptance_criteria: registry lookup performed, prior-match finding stated explicitly
the empty-prefix bypass is reproduced directly with real quoted output (not asserted from the bug report's prose alone)
root cause traced to the specific line/clause in check_prefix/2
confirmed via grep that all current real call sites use non-empty hardcoded prefixes (so the fix is a defense-in-depth guard, not a rescue of an active exploit)
no fix implemented in this step -- diagnosis only, routed to CODE-DESIGNER
